answer.generated: Parameter sharing in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) allows for efficient feature extraction across different locations in an image by applying the same set of learnable parameters (weights) to every receptive field in the image. This mechanism enables the network to detect features such as edges or textures regardless of their position within the image, thereby reducing the number of parameters needed and improving computational efficiency. Consequently, CNNs can generalize well to various spatial arrangements of features, making them particularly effective for tasks involving image recognition and processing.
